title: Making decisions
summary: if / else chains, returning early, replacing long chains with a table, and what counts as true.

sections.heading: The first match wins
body: Conditions are checked from top to bottom and the first one that is true runs. Put the most specific check first.
Returning as soon as you know the answer keeps the code flat: no `else` needed after a `return`.

sections.heading: A table instead of a long chain
body: When every branch has the same shape, put the cases in a list and loop over it. Adding a case is then one new line of data.

sections.heading: What counts as true
body: An `if` accepts any value, not only `true` and `false`. Empty-ish values count as false.
One big difference: an empty list is true in JavaScript but false in Python. To check for "empty" in JavaScript, use `list.length === 0`.

mistakes: Putting a broad check like `n >= 10` before a narrower one like `n >= 100`, so the narrow one never runs.
In Python it is `elif`, not `else if`.
